newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga to get major stake in Sabah body.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga to get major stake in Sabah body.

text.p: State-controlled Tenaga Nasional Bhd will own at least 40 percent as the largest shareholder in the privatised Sabah Electricity Board, Minister of Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Leo Moggie said on Thursday.
"Tenaga will be the lead shareholder," Moggie told reporters after attending a corporate function.
He said that Tenaga's equity stake would be "not less than 40 percent".
Asked how many members the consortium would comprise, Moggie said it would probably be made up of Tenaga, the Sabah state government, as well as two other companies.
He declined to name the two companies, but said, "we have talked with them."
Moggie refused to confirm or deny if one of the companies was Malaysia Mining Corp, but said, "they could possibly be one of the companies."
The Sabah state government has asked for a 30 percent interest in the privatisation, but the Malaysian government was still in discussion about this.
The biggest challenge for the consortium was to immediately upgrade power supply in Sabah as there have been many reports of supply disruptions and related problems, the minister said on Monday.
Moggie said SEB's privatisation would also entail complete restructuring of electricity supply management in Sabah.
